messages:
maria: Heads-up -- after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I see a reproducible ~18% p99 latency regression on qwen2.5 for mixed Japanese/Chinese/English prompts. Looks like more small batches and a fallback to the slower kernel path.
kyle: Can you paste the top-level numbers (p50/p95/p99 + batch-size distribution)?
maria: Quick summary from a 1k-sample perf run on staging (same model binary, only selector change):\n```
p50: 42ms p95: 210ms p99: 486ms\nbatch-size histogram: 1: 62% | 2: 20% | 3-4: 12% | >=5: 6%\nkernel-selected: fast_gpt (was 78%), slow_autokern (now 35% due to fallback)\nKV cache miss-rate (prefix lookups): 17% (up from 3%)\n```\nNotably, prefix KV cache miss-rate jumped which aligns with more small single-token batches.
sunita: hmm. Did you check tokenizer token counts for the mixed-lang prompts? SentencePiece can split CJK+latin combos strangely, producing extra tokens (esp. punctuation + emoji). That can change prefix alignment and cause our cache key (token-offset based) to miss.
maria: Good call. I dumped tokenization for the failing examples: \n```
input: "今日は the API is down。"
tokens: [<ja:今日は>, <space>, <the>, <space>, <API>, <space>, <is>, <space>, <down>, <fullwidth-period>]\ntoken-ids: [3452, 0, 12, 0, 7891, 0, 221, 0, 9981, 40012]\n```
The important bit: mixed scripts insert explicit space tokens and zero-width markers the runtime wasn't normalizing. Our cache key uses `prefix_len_tokens` + `token_offset_bytes` so inconsistent offsets = different keys.
ben: If cache keys are too brittle we could switch to a normalized key (e.g., hash of token id sequence prefix) but that increases hash cost per request. Any profiling on CPU overhead for hashing?
perf-bot: profile uploaded -> https://perf.redwood/internal/1965432100/flame.html (flamegraph + kernel selection trace). Summary: extra ~6ms CPU spent on cache key compares and hash recomputations when batch-size==1. :eyes:
kyle: Another angle: selector change caused kernel to prefer low-latency kernels that assume consistent KV layout; fallback to slow_autokern happens when we detect inconsistent kv-head dims. Can we see the selector decision trace for one failure?
maria: snippet from selector log:\n```
[1965432100.112] selector: input_len=24, avg_seq=28 -> preferred_kernel=fast_gpt\n[1965432100.113] kvcache: prefix_lookup failed (offset_mismatch) -> mark_as_uncached\n[1965432100.114] runtime: fallthrough to slow_autokern (supports per-token fallback path)
```\nSo the selector did choose fast_gpt but kvcache miss forced fallback to slow_autokern which is more expensive per-token.
sunita: Quick hypothesis: tokenizer boundary sensitivity + RoPE scaling adjustment we rolled last month causes token positions to be interpreted differently across kernels (we have legacy-rope vs new-rope scaling modes). If the fast kernel expects normalized rope positions and the cache was built with legacy offsets, the mismatch surfaces only for mixed-script inputs where token-lengths differ per encoding.
ben: Can we validate by forcing rope-scale to 1.0 or pinning kernel to fast_gpt to see if perf recovers? What's the dev command to reproduce locally?
maria: Repro command I used on staging: \n```
redwood-client perf run --model qwen2.5 --batch-seed-file tests/mixed-ja-zh.txt \
  --kernel-selector override=fast_gpt --rope-scale 1.0 --autobatch off
```\nRan that and got p99 down from 486ms -> 422ms (partial win). Forcing `cache-key=token-hash` brought p99 to 410ms but +2ms CPU per request.
kyle: So tradeoff: more robust cache key (token-hash) improves miss-rate and p99 but adds CPU. Could be worth it for mixed-lang heavy tenants.
sunita: Longer-term fix: 1) normalize tokenizer outputs to remove redundant space/zero-width tokens before cache-keying; 2) add a lightweight token-range hash (e.g., 64-bit farmhash) used only when the simple offset-based key fails; 3) add e2e perf test with mixed ja/zh seeds to catch regressions. That should avoid always paying the hash cost.
maria: Agreed. I'll start a PR to: \n- normalize token offsets in the tokenization shim \n- fallback cache-key to 64-bit hash on miss \n- add unit + perf test (mixed lang seeds)\nAssigning: sunita -> tokenizer shim work, kyle -> kernel-selector test harness & test case, ben -> assess CPU cost of farmhash vs siphash, maria -> open PR and wire perf job.
perf-bot: perf job queued -> job 1965432115 (will run mixed-lang perf tests overnight).\n
maria: Thanks all. Filing a regression ticket and will link the PR to the perf job. If anyone wants to pair on the token-normalize patch ping me. :thumbsup:
